title: When The Present Eats The Future | NOEMA
gist: Nathan Gardels argues consumer democracies lack a constituency for the future, while China's planned market-state has captured EVs, batteries and solar. He proposes import quotas with tariffs rather than bans and says democracies should learn from China's long-horizon approach without adopting autocracy.

insights.claim: Consumer democracies have little constituency for the future because politics, culture and markets all reward short-term gratification, from fast fashion to elections to quarterly earnings.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Structural short-termism underpins weak long-horizon industrial investment in the West.
insights.quote: The Achilles heel of consumer democracies is that there is precious little constituency for the future in the present.
